method: Read-only source and saved-status inspection; no consumer code edits, GPU execution, or new runtime reproduction. Selected file fingerprints matched the live checkout after transfer.

findings.fact: Views and fill/copy dispatches bind host integer lengths; GPU counts are tracked separately from logical array descriptors.
Numerical helpers take n::Integer; select_flagged! returns a GPURef count. Scratch is sized from host-known bounds.
ge2sym! passes the GPURef selection result to loose_resize!(...,n::Integer) and Int32(m); source-level incompatible count protocol. This legacy path was not executed in this investigation.
Working retained path uses full-size arrays, -1 sentinels, GPU count views and DeviceRange(count;max=n), rather than propagating array shape.
Dynamic dispatch uses a compiled-capacity grid and GPU count block gating. Count-dependent array dimensions and composed algorithms require additional descriptor/algorithm handling.

Saved report for the latest blocked-sort/precleared combination gives Mantle/libuipc medians 1.760/1.484 ms (128 particles) and 3.084/1.677 ms (512). Exact latest-combination full-frame qualification is still marked pending there. These are prior consumer-reported measurements, not measurements made by this review.
findings.target: P11.G94; compare live/capacity work and complete frame, no speedup claim from one native launch

qualification_status: Specified requirements only; replacement implementation and native tests remain open.
settled_design: One array resource has allocation capacity and GPU-resident logical size (conceptually size::GPURef; specified as Cell/lengthof). Existing head/prepare nodes propagate it into consumers. Consumer integer-only helpers need migration; no new array-shape abstraction.
retracted_inferences: The source-level consumer mismatch does not establish a defect or missing architecture in the proposed Cell/prepare design.
A new public dynamic-view API is not required for kernel-side views from GPU bounds.
A general capacity-overflow publication/retry policy is not a prerequisite for bounded compaction.
The fixed-shape graph-readback baseline and oversized-count KL-05 deserve their existing qualification, not newly invented blockers for basic GPU size tracking.
